Nabu Language

The **Nabu language** is a programming language whose syntax is based on both Java and Kotlin. It is the primary language compiled by the Nabu compiler, and it is designed to interoperate with Java. This is an overview of the language. Individual topics are covered in dedicated pages: - [Classes](/languages/nabu/classes/) - [Fields](/languages/nabu/fields/) - [Generics](/languages/nabu/generics/) - [Annotations](/languages/nabu/annotations/) - [Lambda Expressions](/languages/nabu/lambda-expressions/) - [Exceptions](/languages/nabu/exceptions/) ## A small example ```java package foo.bar.shape; public interface Shape { abstract fun points() : List; } public enum Status { ON("On"), OFF("Off"); private final text : String; private Status(final text : String) { this.text = text; } public fun getText() : String { return text; } } ``` ## Key characteristics - **Type-after-name syntax** (`firstName : String`) similar to Kotlin. - **`fun` keyword** for function declarations. - **Top-level functions** are supported (Nabu-specific, beyond Java). - **Sealed classes, records, enums, and annotations** are all supported. - **Java interoperability** works out of the box — Nabu can call Java and vice versa. ## Grammar The language is defined by ANTLR grammars: - `NabuLexer.g4` - `NabuParser.g4` The AST is built by the `NabuCompilerVisitor` (~3,300 lines) in the `nabu-lang` module.
